entities.summary: The Tegetthoff class was a class of four dreadnought battleships built for the Austro-Hungarian Navy. Named for Austrian Admiral Wilhelm von Tegetthoff, the class was composed of SMS Viribus Unitis, SMS Tegetthoff, SMS Prinz Eugen, and SMS Szent István. Construction started on the ships shortly before World War I; Viribus Unitis and Tegetthoff were both laid down in 1910, Prinz Eugen and Szent István followed in 1912. Three of the four warships were built in the Stabilimento Tecnico Triestino shipyard in Trieste; Szent István was built in the Ganz-Danubius shipyard in Fiume, so that both parts of the Dual Monarchy would participate in the construction of the ships.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Tegetthoff class battleships played a significant role in Austro-Hungarian naval strategy during World War I, with SMS Viribus Unitis serving as a flagship and SMS Tegetthoff participating in the Battle of the North Sea. Although not world-changing, they reflect the military ambitions of the Dual Monarchy.
